advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid computing `attached` twice: either pass only `referencing` into `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` (it already unions attached internally) or drop the internal recompute now that the caller passes the union.
evidence: close_precheck.py:239 passes `landed` as the `referencing` positional arg
close_precheck.py:331 `for sha in attached + list(referencing):` — with referencing now already containing attached, attached is enumerated twice (deduped by `checked` at 332-334)
advisory.finding: `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` recomputes `attached` internally and prepends it to the passed-in commit list, but the caller now passes `landed` (=`attached + referencing`) as that argument, so `_attached_commit_shas` is invoked twice and attached SHAs appear twice in the iteration list. The `checked` set dedups the loop so behavior is correct, but the attached-commit reducer/ticket read is done redundantly.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_check_work_landed`, pass only `referencing` to `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` (which already unions attached internally) and use `landed` solely for the presence gate; or conversely remove the internal `attached` recompute and rename the parameter to reflect it receives the full landed set.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename/re-document the `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` commit parameter to reflect that it may contain the union of attached+referencing SHAs.
evidence: close_precheck.py:239 caller now passes `landed` (attached + referencing) into that parameter
close_precheck.py:339 `if sha not in attached:` relies on the internally recomputed `attached`, not the passed arg, to decide fail-closed vs skip
advisory.finding: The `referencing` parameter of `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` (declared line 303, documented as the referencing-commit scan) is now passed the union of attached+referencing SHAs, so the parameter name and docstring no longer match its contents, obscuring the fail-closed classification that keys off the internally-recomputed `attached`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test passing the same SHA in both `attached` and `referencing` to exercise the new `checked` dedup branch in `_check_file_impact_vs_diff`.
evidence: The `det` fixture (tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py:173) accepts separate `attached=()` and `referencing=()` args, but no test invokes it with the same SHA in both lists — e.g. `det(impact=["src/a.py"], attached=["dup"], referencing=["dup"], paths={"dup": ["src/rogue.py"]})` would exercise the dedup path and should raise exactly once.
src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:339 `if sha not in attached:` (was `if sha in referencing:`)

Existing tests cover unreadable-referencing-only (test_attach_commits.py:217) and unreadable-attached-only (test_attach_commits.py:223), but none passes a SHA in BOTH lists, e.g. `det(impact=["src/a.py"], attached=["both"], referencing=["both"], unreadable=["both"])` — which the new logic skips (no raise) but the old logic blocked.
advisory.finding: The new dedup logic in `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` (`checked: set[str]` / `if sha in checked: continue`) is untested: no test passes the same SHA in both `attached` and `referencing`, so the branch that prevents double-processing a shared SHA is never exercised.
merged_from: The changed unreadable-SHA classification (from `if sha in referencing:` to `if sha not in attached:`) is untested for a SHA present in BOTH attached and referencing. Under the old code such a SHA that is unreadable failed CLOSED (it was in `referencing`); under the new code it is SKIPPED (it IS in `attached`). No test covers this now-changed decision.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `det(impact=["src/a.py"], attached=["dup"], referencing=["dup"], paths={"dup": ["src/rogue.py"]})` and assert a single CommandError naming `dup` and `src/rogue.py`.
